meta.title: Held claims: submitted claims not (yet) on the map
meta.notes: Claims from submissions that were not added to the map. status needs_source = no source found yet; a source can promote it to an edge. status misleading = sources point the other way; kept so it can be revisited. raised_in lists the issue numbers that made the claim, so repeats are counted. Not loaded by the map. raised_in may also name a research branch (e.g. 'grok-v1 branch') instead of an issue number.

statuses.needs_source: No source found that confirms the claim. Send a direct link to promote it.
statuses.misleading: Available sources contradict or do not support the claim as worded.

claims.claim: Batory paid Iustitia 95,000 zł in 2019 for outreach at music festivals and book fairs
claims.checked: Batory's 2019 annual report; only a summary of page 23 could be read, which matches the claim. Needs a word-for-word check of page 23.

claims.claim: Batory gave Iustitia a EUR 50,000 institutional grant in 2022
claims.checked: Batory 2022 annual report pp. 1-37: only a EUR 22,319 project instalment found. The per-grant list of institutional grants was not reached. Re-checked 2026-10-31: still no Iustitia institutional entry in the 2022 report.

claims.claim: The Foundation to Promote Open Society gives Batory about 6.3 million zł a year and is its largest donor
claims.checked: Batory 2019 and 2022 reports name the Open Society donor but give no amounts. Financial statements not yet checked.

claims.claim: The Aequitas judges' association published a tally of Batory money to Iustitia: EUR 156,958 + 95,000 zł
claims.checked: Aequitas document not found. Parts of the tally match Batory reports (2023 EUR 44,639 + 40,000 already on the map; 2022 EUR 22,319 confirmed).

claims.claim: Berek said the Sejm-elected judges have a prepared plan to restore the Tribunal using existing statutory tools, and would not reveal it in advance
claims.checked: Not in OKO.press (11 and 30 Aug 2026) or Interia coverage of his Sejm committee hearing. Sejm committee transcript not checked.

claims.claim: Piotr Serafin, as gatekeeper, unlocked about EUR 137 billion of frozen EU funds for Poland after the 2023 change of government
claims.checked: PAP (18 Sep 2024) calls him gatekeeper for blocking funds under the rule-of-law conditionality mechanism as Budget Commissioner. No source found tying him personally to the unlocking or to the EUR 137bn figure. His tie to Tusk (chief aide 2014-19) is already on the map.

claims.claim: PhD supervisors: Markiewicz - Feliks Zedler (2006); Dziurda - Tadeusz Ereciński (UW 2004); Taborowski - Władysław Czapliński (INP PAN 2011); Berek - Marek Zubik (UW 2016), a former TK judge
claims.checked: Cited Polish Wikipedia page did not resolve when checked 2026-10-31. No other source checked yet.

claims.claim: Bio details: Markiewicz born 8 Jul 1976 in Proszowice; Berek born 12 May 1972, ENA study, PO Sejm candidate 2005; Bentkowska born 1966 in Rzeszów, daughter of Aleksander Bentkowski, DePaul scholarship; Szostek born 21 Mar 1973, PhD 2003, Horizon 2020 grants SHOP4CF and MAS4AI; Korwin-Piotrowska SGH postgraduate years 2004 and 2014
claims.checked: Cited Polish Wikipedia page did not resolve when checked 2026-10-31. Szostek's us.edu.pl profile gives only birth year 1973; Korwin-Piotrowska's SGH studies are confirmed but without years.

claims.claim: Markiewicz sits on the Osiatyński Archive programme council
claims.checked: The re:constitution profile puts Taborowski, not Markiewicz, on the Osiatyński Archive council. Earlier research found Markiewicz only co-authored a 2024 Archive report.

claims.claim: Markiewicz spoke at Batory's Nov 2024 conference on a year of rebuilding the rule of law
claims.checked: Batory's 2024 annual report, the cited source, does not name him or the conference.

claims.claim: Batory paid for repair of the Tour de Konstytucja bus in its 3rd edition
claims.checked: Cited Wyborcza article could not be read (blocked). Batory's 2024 report does show a PLN 154,000 grant to Fundacja Aktywna Demokracja, now on the map.

claims.claim: USAID cooperative agreement 7200AA22CA00025 (about $6.4m) funds Dexis's Central Europe rule-of-law programme
claims.checked: HigherGov lists the $6,389,705 agreement as 'Building Resilience in Civil Society' to undisclosed foreign awardees, which matches GMF's CEBRICS title, and never mentions Dexis.

claims.claim: Watchdog Polska got NED grants of $45,000 and $40,000 and a Dexis/USAID project of PLN 235,385
claims.checked: Watchdog's BIP page could not be read. Advocacy site Proelio says 'over PLN 700k' from NED and PLN 235k via Dexis in 2021-24; needs the primary report.

claims.claim: Batory/EEA money to Themis: PLN 2,389.98 (2016) and PLN 154,989.98 under Active Citizens
claims.checked: Source is an MP's X post that could not be read; the Themis project page failed. The 2014 EEA project itself is on the map.

claims.claim: HFHR received money from GMF's CEBRICS 2023 portfolio
claims.checked: The CEBRICS factsheet names HFHR as an implementation partner, not as a grantee. The partner tie is on the map.

claims.claim: Latarnik Wyborczy was part of a PKO/Orlen-backed 'manipulative campaign'
claims.checked: Cited warsawpoint.com page could not be read. GMF credits the Center for Citizenship Education's 'Electoral Lighthouse' app; that tie is on the map.

claims.claim: Kuisz is president of the Kultura Liberalna Foundation; Wigura is its co-founder
claims.checked: KRS page failed; the site's 'about' page lists Kuisz as editor-in-chief only and says nothing about co-founders.

claims.claim: Journal of Democracy is NED's in-house journal
claims.checked: The journal says it is published by Johns Hopkins University Press; NED holds the article copyright. Mapped with that wording.

claims.claim: Themis founded 2010 as a split from Iustitia; presidents Irena Kamińska 2010-18, Beata Morawiec 2018-24, Korwin-Piotrowska from Aug 2024
claims.checked: Cited Polish Wikipedia page did not resolve when checked 2026-10-31.

claims.claim: At the Dom Sędziego Seniora founding, Iustitia was represented by Maciej Strączyński and Jolanta Korwin-Piotrowska, Themis by Irena Kamińska
claims.checked: The foundation page lists founders and Kamińska as board vice-president but not who represented each founder; Kwartalnik Iustitia lists Jolanta Korwin-Piotrowska on the first council only. No family tie to Anna Korwin-Piotrowska is documented.

claims.claim: The prosecutor's statement reproduces Patyra's panel allegations for TK cases K 3/26, Kpt 1/26, U 2/26 and K 22/26
claims.checked: The 1 Oct 2026 prosecutor statement names no TK case numbers and no specific panels. The case list may come from another document; none was cited.

claims.claim: On 30 Oct 2026 Korwin-Piotrowska issued a separate order imposing a one-month break in duties on Vice-President Sochański
claims.checked: The TK information page title names both Święczkowski and Sochański, but the page and the order PDFs could not be read (blocked). Needs a readable copy or press report.

claims.claim: The 30 Oct order invokes art. 12(4)/11(2) TK Act, art. 130(1) common courts law, art. 10(1) Supreme Court Act and art. 19/30 TK judges status act, and lists seven grounds (assembly and 2027 budget, five judges not admitted, ECHR interim measure of 5 May 2026, outsiders at Berek's oath, political statements, panel order, delays)
claims.checked: Order PDFs blocked to automated reading. The map already carries Patyra's note giving the main reasons. Needs a readable copy.

claims.claim: NIK (Supreme Audit Office) put funding for the PFN system at PLN 633m+ through 2026
claims.checked: Not in the Polsat (15 Jul 2026) or OKO.press (2017) articles. The cited Polskie Radio article could not be read.

claims.claim: PLN 8.43m is the amount of the Fair Courts campaign
claims.checked: Prosecutors give 'at least PLN 8.4m' as alleged damage to PFN, not the campaign cost. OKO.press put the campaign budget at about PLN 10m.

claims.claim: Former Solvere board members Anna P. and Piotr M. were detained in the PFN investigation
claims.checked: TVP (23 Sep 2026) confirms CBA detained 'Piotr M. and Anna P.' on the Rzeszów prosecutor's order, but does not name Solvere. Linking them to Solvere is an inference from founders' initials. Private individuals: not mapped without a source naming the link.
